clue.text: Elevating caricature

explanation.surface: A satirical cartoon that lifts the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's take-off is its rising from the ground, and a take-off is also a mocking impression or parody.

clue.text: Exchange foreign currency for this device

parts.note: to exchange goods is to trade
the mark was the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: A money-changer swaps foreign notes in return for some gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A device in the heraldic sense is an emblem, and a trademark is a firm's registered emblem.

clue.text: Opening filled for a turn in the opening act

definitions.text: Opening filled for a turn in the opening act

parts.words: Opening filled for a turn in the opening act
parts.note: the opening in a door that a key fills and is turned in when the door is to be opened

explanation.surface: A gap in a theatre bill is filled by a performer's turn in the first act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' and 'act' suggest the stage, but the turn is a key turning and the act is opening a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hole in a lock into which a key is put and turned.

clue.text: Stonewalling — bats with toe, in new position

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new position, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: A stubborn cricket batsman, bat beside his toe, shuffles to a new stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins BATS and TOE; 'in' is part of the fodder, and 'new position' rearranges all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewalling is stubborn blocking and refusal to budge, the behaviour of someone unyielding.

clue.text: Thin skin? That's the picture

explanation.surface: A sensitive person's touchiness is the whole story.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is a thin layer or coating, and a film is also a movie.

clue.text: Turn of the century, second hand cameras so adjusted

indicators.note: turn tells us the little word of is turned round

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for century (Roman numeral 100)
second-hand goods are used

explanation.surface: Around 1900, second-hand cameras were sold already set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of the century' reads as a date, but 'Turn' reverses 'of' and 'the century' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera whose lens has been adjusted to give a sharp image is brought into focus.

clue.text: Needed by Noah for nocturnal navigation ?

definitions.text: Needed by Noah for nocturnal navigation

parts.words: Needed by Noah for nocturnal navigation
parts.note: Noah sailed his ark on the Flood, so a lamp for night sailing would be his deluge lamp

explanation.surface: Noah's ark would want a lamp to sail by at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as FLOOD LIGHT: the light Noah needed on the Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful lamp throwing broad bright illumination, here read as a lamp for the biblical deluge.

clue.text: River is around about the best

indicators.note: the river's name is around, that is wraps, the next piece

parts.note: the Cam is the river at Cambridge
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A river flows round in roughly the finest way.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream is the choicest part of anything, as cream is the richest part of milk.

clue.text: Set out to guard the attendant

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of set are put out of order

parts.note: to ward is to guard, as in ward off

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to keep watch over the attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an attendant on a ship or aircraft, or the officer managing an estate.

clue.text: Editor returns enemy of the writer

indicators.note: returns means the abbreviation for editor goes back the other way

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: An editor comes back to confront the author's adversary.
explanation.walkthrough: Daniel DEFOE wrote Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was an English novelist, author of Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Jack may end with his vessel in the deep

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor

indicators.note: the end of the word may is its final letter

parts.note: SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: A sailor may finish up with his ship at the bottom of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a sailor (jack tar), giving AB; 'may end' is the last letter of 'may'.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a poetic name for the ocean depths, and an abyss is a bottomless chasm.

clue.text: Autumn notebook ?

parts.note: in autumn the trees' foliage comes free, so an autumnal notebook would be one whose pages come free

explanation.surface: A diary kept through the season of falling leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: A notebook with detachable pages is described by the state of trees in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A notebook whose sheets are separate and can be removed, as foliage is detached in autumn.

clue.text: Foreign cox has tie twisted

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of the two words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An overseas rowing cox wears his tie askew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' only links COX and TIE, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic means coming from or characteristic of a distant country.

clue.text: Drink of paradise

parts.note: the only drink the first man in Eden had was plain water

explanation.surface: Nectar served in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam in the Garden of Eden had only water to drink, so water is jocularly called Adam's ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous old name for water, the only beverage available to the first man in Eden.

clue.text: Well before the time of high water

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: a spring is a well, a source of water
tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: A well dug in advance of the flood season.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring tide is the highest tide of the month, near new and full moon.

clue.text: Hare naturally runs in this sporting centre

indicators.note: in shows the answer lies within the words Hare naturally

explanation.surface: A hare runs wild around this stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' only joins; the answer sits inside 'hARE NAturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed area for sport or entertainment.

clue.text: Out-crop mined in Wales perhaps

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A rock outcrop mined in the Welsh hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-crop' looks like a geology word, but 'Out' is the anagram signal on CROP and MINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wales is a principality, a territory ruled by a prince, which is a princedom.

clue.text: Queen shows many a' sign to, encourage the 'painter

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
Leo is a sign of the zodiac
to pat someone on the back is to encourage them
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A queen displays many signs of urging on the artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' gives C (100) and RA is a Royal Academician; the OCR's stray quote marks are not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was queen of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: One by the way solid 'and informative

definitions.text: One by the way solid 'and informative

parts.words: One by the way solid 'and informative
parts.note: a marker standing at the roadside, made of rock, telling travellers the distance

explanation.surface: Incidentally, one is sound and full of facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like 'incidentally', but means beside the road, where such a stone marker stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside stone marking the distance in miles to a place.

clue.text: Frolicsome nature of Dinah's offspring.

parts.note: Dinah is Alice's cat in Lewis Carroll's books, so her offspring are young cats, and their nature is playful

explanation.surface: A playful character inherited by Dinah's children.
explanation.walkthrough: Dinah is Alice's cat in Alice in Wonderland, so her young are kittens.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful and lively in the manner of a young cat.

clue.text: Prohibited old army having soundly disapproved

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's long-standing volunteer reserve
to boo is to show disapproval noisily

explanation.surface: The veterans' regiment was banned after a jeering crowd showed their displeasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by custom or rule is taboo, and to taboo something is to ban it.

clue.text: She sounds a bit -alcoholic

indicators.note: sounds shows the answer is said like another word

parts.note: ethyl is the chemical group forming part of ethyl alcohol, the alcohol in drinks

explanation.surface: She sounds as if she has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Ethyl alcohol is the alcohol in drink; said aloud it is the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a woman's name, so it can stand for the pronoun for a female.

clue.text: Pays tribute to aces sometimes

explanation.surface: A card player salutes his aces now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour someone is to pay tribute to them; in bridge the ace, king, queen, jack and ten of trumps are the honour cards.

clue.text: Undermine-shifting boats before time

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second
shifting signals the letters of boats are moved about

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Moving boats ahead of schedule wrecks the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges BOATS into SABOT, which goes before AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sabotage is to wreck or undermine deliberately.

clue.text: As if nothing is changed — capital

indicators.note: is changed signals the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: As if nothing has changed in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing' gives O, which joins the letters of 'As if' to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Giant bird, and tail-less

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: tail-less means the word and loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A huge bird that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and tail-less' is AND without its last letter, AN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giants of Greek myth, and a titan is any person or thing of great size.

clue.text: They provide the backing bookmakers need

definitions.text: They provide the backing bookmakers need

parts.words: They provide the backing bookmakers need
parts.note: read the makers as those who make books: bound volumes need a back

explanation.surface: Gamblers' stakes are what the bookies require.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' and 'bookmakers' suggest betting, but the books are bound volumes needing a back.
explanation.definitionFit: The backs of bound books, where the pages are joined.

clue.text: Simple lady's table centre

parts.note: her is the possessive for a lady

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the word table

explanation.surface: A plain woman's dining table centrepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'simple' is an old name for a medicinal plant, so it is a noun here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is a medicinal plant used on its own, in other words a herb.

clue.text: Severe effect of a cold snack?

definitions.text: Severe effect of a cold snack?

parts.words: Severe effect of a cold snack
parts.note: read cold as freezing weather and snack as a nibble: injury from a nip of the cold

explanation.surface: A chilled snack can have serious consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer FROST BITE: a 'bite' (snack) of frost (cold).
explanation.definitionFit: Injury to body tissue caused by freezing, as if the cold had taken a nibble.

clue.text: Some trip to our new place in the West

indicators.note: some means only part of the word trip is used
new means the letters of our are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A holiday trip to our new home in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some trip' is TR, part of 'trip'; 'to' just links; 'new' rearranges OUR to URO.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is the cathedral city of Cornwall, in the far south-west of England.

clue.text: Musical instruction from an erstwhile poet

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the medieval Italian poet

explanation.surface: Directions on a score taken from an old poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a tempo marking telling players to go at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: One kind of band that is likely to make the ball go

definitions.text: likely to make the ball go

parts.note: a brass band is one kind of band
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A band whose music sends the ball dance spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: A brassie is an old golf club, the number two wood, so 'the ball' is a golf ball, not a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie is an old wooden golf club with a brass sole, used to drive the golf ball a long way.
